cells.gaps: The share is for 2021, printed as a rate without its counts, covers all facilities and not primary clinics alone, and nothing newer is held; WHO's annual report gives 89.2% for the same year (TGO-021). TGO-026 records no coordinated digital health strategy across the systems while the PNDS monitoring plan 2023-2027 (TGO-031) names DHIS2 and runs past the as-at; no domestic budget line is stated, and community entry into DHIS2 is a procedure requirement, not an observed count.
cells.note: Facility entry at the primary tier with more than half of facilities keying their own reports meets the whole of rung 4, and the ministry owns the system under a current plan, so the cap does not apply. Rung 5 needs 90 per cent or more on a figure published within two years, and the only share was published in October 2023 for 2021.

cells.gaps: The statement of absence is that no electronic health record system was established at December 2025 and that none of about 335 insurance-contracted facilities held one; it does not say in terms that records are on paper at every tier, and it does not cover facilities outside the insurance scheme. Where records are digitised is not held: the only rows on it (TGO-004, TGO-005) are from the excluded source.
cells.note: Rung 2 needs some hospitals or pilot facilities using a record system, or a national system procured, and the evidence gives a pilot that is planned and financed but not started. The dated World Bank baseline of no system and zero facilities is taken as the statement of absence.
